chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Isma'il ibn al-Hurr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the crescent moon sets before the twilight, it is for that night; and when it sets after the twilight, it is for two nights."

key_terms.اَلشَّفَقِ: Twilight (the reddish glow in the sky after sunset)

ai.seo_question: How does the setting of the crescent moon relative to twilight determine the validity of a month's sighting in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the astronomical criteria for lunar month inauguration, distinguishing between a 'true' new moon (visible before twilight) and a 'false' one (visible after twilight). In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction ensures that the sighting is not merely an optical illusion caused by the moon's position relative to the sun, thereby validating the start of fasting or Eid with greater precision.
